title: Coal Miners Face Long Legal Battles for Health Support
subtitle: As cases of black lung disease hit a 50-year high, retired miners struggle to secure federal benefits against company appeals.

summary.en: Cases of black lung disease are at their highest level in nearly 50 years. Many retired coal miners are finding it difficult to get federal health benefits. Coal companies frequently challenge these claims in court, leading to years of waiting. Families say the process is unfair and puts a heavy burden on sick workers. New government reports highlight these delays and the difficulties miners face in proving their illness.
summary.zh: 黑肺病病例數已達近五十年來最高水準。許多退休煤礦工人發現難以取得聯邦健康補助。煤礦公司經常在法庭上挑戰這些索賠申請，導致礦工需等待多年。家屬表示此過程極不公平，對病患造成沉重負擔。新的政府報告凸顯了這些延誤，以及礦工在證明病情時所面臨的困難。

paragraphs.en: For many retired coal miners in the United States, the fight for their health is becoming just as difficult as the years they spent working underground. Recent data shows that cases of black lung disease—a permanent lung condition caused by breathing in coal dust—have reached their highest level in nearly 50 years. While this health crisis grows, many former workers are trapped in a long and stressful legal process to receive the federal benefits they need to survive.
paragraphs.zh: 對於許多美國退休煤礦工人來說，爭取健康權益的過程，變得與他們過去在地底工作的歲月一樣艱辛。最新數據顯示，黑肺病（一種因吸入煤塵而導致的永久性肺部疾病）的病例數已達到近五十年來的最高水準。在這場健康危機日益嚴重的同時，許多前礦工卻陷入了漫長且充滿壓力的法律程序中，難以取得維持生計所需的聯邦補助。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian Business, the federal black lung program was created in 1969 to provide money and medical support to miners who can no longer work due to this disease. However, the system is currently failing many of those it was designed to help. A report from the government accountability office (GAO) released in May found that between 2013 and 2024, 40 percent of approved claims were challenged by coal companies. These companies often use the appeals process to delay or stop payments, leaving miners to wait years for a final decision.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報商業版》（The Guardian Business）報導，聯邦黑肺病計畫於一九六九年設立，旨在為因罹患此病而無法繼續工作的礦工提供資金與醫療援助。然而，該制度目前卻未能照顧到許多它本應協助的對象。美國政府稽核處（GAO）於五月發布的一份報告指出，在二零一三至二零二四年期間，有百分之四十的核准申請遭到煤礦公司提出異議。這些公司經常利用上訴程序來拖延或阻止給付，導致礦工必須等待多年才能獲得最終裁決。

paragraphs.en: Josh Armes, a 74-year-old retired miner from Virginia, is one of many people caught in this system. After working in the mines for 38 years, he was diagnosed with black lung disease. For the past four years, he has relied on an oxygen tank to breathe. Despite his clear medical diagnosis, he has been fighting to keep his federal benefits for 12 years because a coal company appealed his case. His daughter, Crystal Armes, explained that the process is extremely difficult. She noted that families are often forced to pay for expensive medical tests themselves and must find lawyers just to prove their case. She argued that the current law is unfair because it allows companies to challenge benefits even after they have been awarded.
paragraphs.zh: 來自維吉尼亞州的七十四歲退休礦工亞姆斯（Josh Armes），正是受困於此制度的眾多受害者之一。他在礦場工作三十八年後被診斷出罹患黑肺病，過去四年來，他必須依賴氧氣瓶才能呼吸。儘管有明確的醫療診斷，但他為了保住聯邦補助，已經抗爭了十二年，原因是一家煤礦公司對他的案件提出了上訴。他的女兒克莉絲朵（Crystal Armes）解釋，這個過程極其困難。她指出，家庭往往被迫自行支付昂貴的醫療檢測費用，還必須聘請律師才能證明自己的權益。她認為現行法律極不公平，因為它允許公司在補助核准後仍能提出挑戰。

paragraphs.en: The GAO report highlighted a troubling trend in how these companies handle claims. Many miners told investigators that they feel coal operators are simply waiting for them to die or to give up so the companies can avoid paying. The report found that between January 2013 and mid-August 2024, 390 people who were initially told they would receive benefits had their claims denied after a company appeal. In these cases, the miners were even forced to pay back the money they had already received. On average, an appealed claim takes three years or more to resolve.
paragraphs.zh: 政府稽核處的報告凸顯了這些公司處理索賠案件時的一種令人不安的趨勢。許多礦工向調查人員表示，他們感覺煤礦業者只是在等他們過世或放棄，好讓公司能規避賠償責任。報告發現，在二零一三年一月至二零二四年八月中旬期間，有三百九十名原本獲准領取補助的人，在公司提出上訴後被撤銷資格。在這些案例中，礦工甚至被迫償還已經領取的款項。平均而言，一件上訴案件需要三年或更久的時間才能解決。

paragraphs.en: This situation is happening at a time when the coal industry is receiving new support from the Trump administration. While the government aims to boost coal production, health experts and lawmakers are concerned about the rising number of sick workers. According to The Guardian Business, a group of Democratic senators—including Mark Warner, John Hickenlooper, Tim Kaine, and John Fetterman—have introduced new legislation. They hope these changes will improve the benefits system and make it easier for miners to get the help they deserve without facing years of legal pressure.
paragraphs.zh: 這種情況發生的同時，煤炭產業正獲得川普（Donald Trump）政府的新支持。儘管政府目標是提升煤炭產量，但健康專家與國會議員對病患人數的攀升感到憂心。根據《衛報商業版》報導，包括華納（Mark Warner）、希肯魯柏（John Hickenlooper）、凱恩（Tim Kaine）以及費特曼（John Fetterman）在內的一群民主黨參議員，已提出新的法案。他們希望這些變革能改善補助制度，讓礦工能更輕易地獲得應有的協助，而不必面臨長年的法律壓力。

paragraphs.en: For families like the Armes family, the wait continues. Josh Armes expressed his frustration with a system that seems to ignore his medical reality. He pointed out that he has official papers confirming his condition, yet he is still denied support. He asked, “Do you have to be dead?” to receive the help that was promised to him. As the number of black lung cases continues to rise, the debate over how to protect these workers remains a major issue. For now, thousands of miners and their families remain in a state of uncertainty, waiting for a system that many feel is designed to work against them rather than for them.
paragraphs.zh: 對於像亞姆斯這樣的家庭來說，等待仍在持續。亞姆斯對於一個似乎無視他醫療現況的制度感到挫折。他指出，自己擁有確認病情的官方文件，卻仍被拒絕提供支援。他質問道：「難道非得要死了才能得到當初承諾的幫助嗎？」隨著黑肺病病例持續增加，關於如何保護這些工人的爭論仍是一項重大議題。目前，數以千計的礦工及其家庭仍處於不確定的狀態，等待著一個在許多人眼中，設計初衷是為了對抗他們而非協助他們的制度。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To be stuck in a difficult situation from which it is hard to escape.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見指被物理困住，這裡指陷入法律困境。文中：many former workers are trapped in a long and stressful legal process to receive the federal benefits they need to survive.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To formally question the truth or legality of a decision or claim.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見指挑戰某人，這裡指在法律程序中提出異議。文中：40 percent of approved claims were challenged by coal companies.
常見指物理上的推舉，這裡指提升產業產量。文中：While the government aims to boost coal production, health experts and lawmakers are concerned about the rising number of sick workers.

previousArticles.title: Coal Miners Fight for Health Benefits as Lung Disease Cases Rise
previousArticles.summaryEn: Cases of black lung disease among coal miners have reached a nearly 50-year high. Many retired workers are struggling to get federal benefits due to long and difficult legal appeals. Coal companies often challenge these claims, forcing miners to wait years for financial and medical support. A recent government report highlights that thousands of miners face delays and financial stress during this process. Lawmakers are now looking at new ways to improve the system for these workers.

quiz.question: According to the GAO report, what happens to some miners after a coal company successfully appeals their initial benefit approval?

options.A: They are required to undergo additional medical testing at the company's expense.
options.B: They must return the financial support they had previously been granted.
options.C: They are automatically enrolled in a different federal health program.
options.D: They are granted a faster review process for their next application.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第四段，報告指出在 2013 年至 2024 年間，有 390 名原本獲准領取補助的礦工在公司上訴後被撤銷資格，且被迫退還已領取的款項。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到家屬常需自費進行昂貴檢測；選項 C 文章未提及；選項 D 與文意相反，上訴過程通常會拖延數年而非加速。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why might coal companies prefer to challenge benefit claims through the legal system?

options.A: They believe that most miners are misdiagnosed by their doctors.
options.B: They want to ensure that only the most severe cases receive federal funding.
options.C: They aim to reduce costs by exhausting the miners' resources and time.
options.D: They are legally required to verify every claim to prevent government fraud.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第四段提到礦工認為公司是在「等待他們過世或放棄」，且平均上訴需耗時三年以上，顯示公司利用法律程序來拖延支付，迫使礦工因經濟壓力或健康惡化而放棄。選項 A 並無根據；選項 B 是公司可能宣稱的藉口，但非文章推論出的核心動機；選項 D 文中未提及這是法律強制要求，而是公司主動挑戰的行為。

quiz.question: In the phrase 'the system is currently failing many of those it was designed to help,' what does the word 'failing' imply?

options.A: The system is not performing its intended function effectively.
options.B: The system has completely stopped operating due to a lack of funds.
options.C: The system has been declared illegal by the government.
options.D: The system is being replaced by a new, more efficient program.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此語境中，「failing」並非指系統崩潰（stop operating），而是指該系統無法達成其設立初衷（提供補助給患病礦工），未能提供應有的協助。選項 B 錯誤，系統仍在運作但效率不彰；選項 C 文章未提到系統違法；選項 D 雖然國會議員正推動新法，但原系統並未被宣告替換，僅是功能失靈。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article regarding the current situation for retired coal miners?

options.A: The coal industry is expanding rapidly, leading to more jobs for younger workers.
options.B: Medical technology has advanced enough to cure most cases of black lung disease.
options.C: New legislation will immediately resolve all financial disputes for retired miners.
options.D: Retired miners face significant obstacles in accessing promised benefits due to corporate legal challenges.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。本文主旨聚焦於患有黑肺病的退休礦工在申請聯邦補助時，面臨煤礦公司利用法律程序惡意拖延或拒絕支付的困境，這也是文章反覆強調的社會議題。選項 A 與本文焦點無關；選項 B 與事實不符，文章提到這是永久性肺病；選項 C 過於樂觀，文章僅提到議員希望改善，而非問題已立即解決。
